title: A character's elite credentials lend a movement mainstream weight but mark them as too privileged to represent it
body:
- Using elite credentials can legitimize a cause to mainstream audiences by lending it institutional authority and counter-narrative weight.
- The same credentials risk making the character appear too privileged or disconnected from the grassroots base.
- The tension persists because whatever authority the credentials carry comes from the same status that marks the character as an outsider to the cause.
- The character must choose between strategic reach (leveraging the credentials for institutional access) and authentic representation (staying grounded in the movement).
- Case: Jo faces this choice between leveraging her elite credentials to legitimize the movement and risking dismissal as too privileged to represent it.
conversion: The same elite credentials that legitimize a character as a spokesperson for a movement disqualify them as a representative of it.
